title: Bit Manipulation
summary: Work directly with the 0s and 1s inside a number to save space and solve pairing puzzles.
keyPoints: A bit is 0 or 1; an integer is a row of bits with place values 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on.
XOR returns 1 only when the bits differ, and `x ^ x = 0`, `x ^ 0 = x`.
AND masks select bits; OR sets bits; shifts move bits left or right.
XOR is the standard trick for finding the one value that appears an odd number of times.

complexity.note: `x &= x - 1` clears the lowest set bit.

commonMistakes: Using XOR to pair values when more than one value appears an odd number of times.
Confusing logical `&&` with bitwise `&`, or `||` with `|`.
Assuming JavaScript bitwise operators work on integers wider than 32 bits; they do not.
Forgetting operator precedence and writing a mask expression without parentheses.
interviewNotes: Say how many bits the values use and whether the language's bitwise operators are fixed-width.
For XOR problems, state the cancellation rule and why the remaining value is the answer.
For masks, name the purpose of each bit instead of using unexplained magic numbers.

checkYourself.question: Why does XORing every value find the one unpaired value?
checkYourself.answer: Every pair cancels to zero. The unpaired value remains because zero XOR the value is the value.

checkYourself.question: What does `x & (x - 1)` do?
checkYourself.answer: It clears the lowest set bit of x. Repeating it counts set bits in time proportional to the number of 1s.

checkYourself.question: How do you check whether bit i is set?
checkYourself.answer: Shift the bit down and mask it: `(x >> i) & 1`. The result is 0 or 1.
